stem: During transfer to the PACU, the handoff report does not include the client's estimated blood loss, intraoperative complications, or medications given during anesthesia. What should the PACU nurse do?

options.A: Accept the incomplete handoff because these details can be reviewed later if the client becomes unstable
options.B: Clarify the missing information with the transferring team before the handoff is completed because it can affect immediate postoperative assessment and care
options.C: Ask the client to provide the missing intraoperative information after fully awakening from anesthesia
options.D: Document that the information was unavailable and omit further follow-up because responsibility transfers to the PACU at arrival

rationale: Immediate postoperative care depends on an accurate handoff from the operating-room/anesthesia team. Important handoff content includes anesthesia type and duration, medications and IV fluids, estimated blood loss, urine output, drains, and intraoperative complications. Missing information that may change PACU assessment or intervention should be clarified with the transferring team rather than deferred, reconstructed from the recovering client, or simply documented as unavailable.
educational_objective: The PACU nurse ensures that transfer-of-care communication includes clinically significant intraoperative information and resolves missing data that may affect immediate postoperative management before handoff is completed.
source_locator: 2.5 Postoperative Nursing Care — Care in the Post-Anesthesia Care Unit or Intensive Care Unit; Transfer to Medical-Surgical Unit — critical handoff components including anesthesia type/duration, IV fluids/medications, estimated blood loss, drain output and intraoperative complications
source_claim_supported: The chapter states that the PACU RN requires clear, thorough handoff information and lists clinically important intraoperative data needed to manage recovery and complications.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — Collaboration with Multidisciplinary Team and Continuity of Care, printed p. 21 (PDF page 24): identify significant information to report to other disciplines; provide and receive handoff of care; follow up on unresolved issues regarding client care
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — handoff communication and continuity of care
correction_summary: Replaced PACU-nurse role-definition trivia with a transition-of-care scenario that requires recognition and resolution of missing intraoperative information. Retained the source category but strengthened NCLEX relevance and distractor plausibility.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: NCBI perioperative nursing chapter reviewed; handoff components and need for clear OR-to-PACU communication verified.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: EBL, medications/fluids and intraoperative complications are explicitly listed as handoff components.
audit_findings.choice_A: Unsafe delay in obtaining clinically relevant information.
audit_findings.choice_B: Correct; resolves missing data at transition of care.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; the recovering client is not an appropriate source for intraoperative details.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; unresolved clinically significant information requires follow-up.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B establishes safe, complete handoff before transfer responsibility is finalized.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address handling of incomplete handoff information.
audit_findings.blueprint: Direct NCSBN 2026 Management of Care continuity/handoff mapping.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked whether care must literally be delayed for every missing datum; stem specifies high-impact missing intraoperative information, preserving B as uniquely best.
